a: Bubble sort repeatedly swaps adjacent out-of-order pairs; simple but slow O(n²).
Insertion sort builds a sorted prefix by inserting each next element.
Mergesort divides, sorts halves, and merges; O(n log n) stable.
Quicksort partitions around a pivot; average O(n log n).
Heapsort uses a binary heap for O(n log n) time in place.
A stable sort keeps equal keys in original relative order.
Linear search checks each element until it finds the target.
Arrays store elements in contiguous memory with O(1) index access.
Linked lists store nodes with pointers; inserts are easy, random access is not.
Trees organize hierarchical data with parent-child links.
